parts.why: Both forms: 'Circle 10' can be heard as 'circle the 10' printed in '10 +', and K children do exactly that. Say 'Circle ten squares.' The key should also show the ring around two full columns, the first thing a teacher checks (lesson note). Keys 6|16 and 5|15 are right.
A 17 = 10 + 7, B 19 = 10 + 9; dots counted on the page. Fine.
A 16 and 15, B 18 and 11; the key fills the first frame first. Fine.
A 8 and 3, B 4 and 2; one answer each.
Keys right (A 14, 26, 38; B 25, 32, 40). Minor: the chart shows 11-40 in both forms and never reaches 50, the lesson's number; show 21-50 if the generator allows.

The hidden number is printed in part 7 on the same page (A: 42 is the first box of part 7 card 2; B: 79 is printed in part 7 card 1). No part of either form reaches 100 although the unit is 'Counting to 100'. Show 71-100 in one form's chart and keep part 7 outside the chart's range.

Strong tell: part 6's chart, directly above, prints the strip answers. A: 48, 49, 50 (card 2) and 70 (card 1); B: 72, 78, 80 (card 1) and 51, 52 (card 2). Take strips from ranges no chart shows (A 81-100; B 41-50 or 81-100) and never leave three blanks in a row.

Form A hides 70 in both strips (30, 70 and 40, 70), and 70 is also part 7's answer, so it gets copied. No strip in either form reaches 100. A card 2: hide 40 and 60; end one strip in each form at 100.
Arrows measured on the ticks: A 2, 13, 17; B 3, 12, 15. Keys right.

A hides three mid-row cells (43, 56, 68); B hides two row-end cells (51 first in its row, 70 last), which need the down-the-column pattern and are harder. Give each form one row-end blank and two mid-row blanks.
Keys right (70/72, 32/52; 67/69, 28/48). Small arrows from the middle number out to each box would stop a child reading '[ ] -1 71' as '? - 1 = 71' and writing 72 on the left.

Tell in both forms: the by-5s strip prints the by-10s strip's blanks (A and B card 2 print 60 and 70) and the by-10s strip prints a by-5s blank (A prints 80, B prints 90). Blank positions are identical in A and B. Pick ranges that do not overlap; move B's blanks.

Keys right (184 + 216 = 400, 136 + 785 = 921, both make a new ten and a new hundred; carry boxes print over every place, so no tell). One problem only, so one slip decides the part: add a second that makes only one new ten or hundred, as the lesson objective says.
Keys right (675 - 180 = 495, 728 - 156 = 572); both regroup a hundred only. One problem only: add a second that regroups a ten for the ones (e.g., A 463 - 128, B 572 - 236).
500 - 137 = 363 and 900 - 269 = 631, both across two zeros. Fine.
Whale 0 to 6 and watermelon 0 to 7 measured on the ruler; keys right.

Form B card 1 is form A card 2 exactly (same ribbon, 4 clips, 2 craft sticks), and both B ribbons are 4 clips long, so '4' repeats inside B. Give B card 1 a new length (e.g., 3 clips, 9 cubes). The earlier finding (right circle always the bottom one) is fixed.
Keys right (skateboard 7 - plane 4 = 3; stapler 4 - book 3 = 1). B's difference of 1 is easier than A's 3; prefer a difference of 2-4 in both.

Same ribbon story, same picture, and B (72 - 20) needs no regrouping while A (75 - 28) does, so B is easier. B: 'A garden hose is 83 feet long. Dad cuts off 47 feet. How long is the hose now?' (36). Key: accept 28 + 47 = 75. Earlier key finding fixed: the bar shows '?'.

A card 2 is 12:30, a Grade 1 half hour; A has no time after the half hour, the lesson's own watch point. Both card 1s are 9:05/9:10 and B offers 9:10, A's answer, as a foil. A card 2: e.g., 2:50 with 3:50 as a foil; B 5:35: add 6:35 as a foil.

Coins are circles with their value printed, already sorted largest first: the part checks adding 25, 10, 5 and 1, not knowing the coins or ordering them (the lesson's two errors). 'Purse' names nothing drawn. Draw coin faces without numerals in mixed order (or at least name each coin); see question 4.

Keys right. A card 1 (25 + 45) regroups; A card 2 and both B cards do not, so A is harder. Give B one regrouping total (e.g., coconut 35 cents + apple 45 cents). A prices wild animals (wolf, moose, orangutan) at 10-45 cents; use toys or food, as B does.

Each card shows one shape per number (3, 4 and 6 each right exactly once), so the last shape is found by elimination; no five-sided shape appears though the lesson sorts pentagons. Offer 3, 4, 5, 6 under every shape and draw the shapes independently, repeats allowed. The chips nearly touch; space them.
Keys right (square pyramid 5, cube 6). The lesson is faces, edges, and vertices; the check asks faces only, one card. Add one edges or corners card per form.
Giraffe X, dragonfly check, watermelon slice check, mango X; each defensible only one way. Direction is now US wording (earlier finding fixed).
Every key mirror checked cell by cell: tulip 23, umbrella 20, crab 22, sun 25 squares. A and B are even.
One match in each form (A third box, B fourth); the other two are turned or flipped. Direction as recommended (earlier finding fixed).
Three-digit numbers now (earlier finding fixed): A 840, 480, 790; B 910, 390, 540; each form has one ones-digit-5 case. Write-in boxes, so no answer positions.
A 300, 900, 600; B 700, 400, 800; each has one tens-digit-5 case. Earlier position finding fixed.

Keys right; earlier repeats fixed (no 43, no fives). Both card 2s still total 60. Only B card 1 (16 + 68: 90, but the exact 84 rounds to 80) separates rounding first from rounding the sum; give A one such item too.

Keys right; three answer boxes and the new direction (earlier findings fixed). B's third (502 - 147) subtracts across a zero, A's (612 - 266) does not, so B is harder: make A's third across a zero (e.g., 603 - 258). The key leaves the carry box of 160 + 656 empty.

One odd/even item per form: a guess passes half the time. Both forms start with 343. Give 3-4 sums per form with both outcomes and new numbers in B. Earlier finding (ringed square, sums past 1,000) is fixed.

All four strips go down by 7, and A card 2 is the 7s facts backward. Use a different step per card (e.g., 6 and 9) and one growing pattern (the lesson also has G3-326). 'Write the missing ones' can mean ones digits here: say 'missing numbers'.

In all four cards the answer is the earlier of a one-minute pair (8:48/8:49, 1:33/1:34, 10:28/10:29, 7:22/7:23): pick the earlier and win. No foil catches the lesson's errors (nearest five, next hour). For 8:48 offer 8:48, 8:50, 9:48; vary which neighbor is right.

Whole hours only (8:00 to 10:00; 4:00 to 7:00), not crossing 12: Grade 2 work. 3.MD.A.1 measures intervals in minutes. Use the level that crosses 12 and add a minutes card per form (e.g., 3:15 to 3:50 = 35 minutes), unit after the box. See question 1.

A adds 2 whole hours to 5:00; B adds 1 hour 30 minutes to 1:00: uneven, and neither crosses an hour with minutes (the lesson's 3:45 + 30 minutes). Use the quarter-hour level, every card crossing the hour. Write '2 hours', not '2 h'.

Every mark is labelled and the liquid stops on a label (10, 25), so it checks reading a printed number, not the scale's step (the lesson's skill). Celsius only is wrong for a US check. Use degrees F (G3-476), marks by 2 labelled every 10, reading between labels. See question 2.
450 g, 350 g, 500 g, 400 g; the weights add up and the masses are believable.

Readings right (750, 1,250, on unlabeled marks: good). The unit is printed 'ml' at the scale and after the box; US is 'mL' (the worksheet title already says 2,000 mL). One card per form only; a second cup would steady the part.

checks.why: Every key is right. Part 6's chart prints part 7's answers on the same page in both forms; fix that, the repeated 70 in part 8 and the 'Circle 10' wording, and let one part reach 100.
Keys right and grade fit good. Part 4's strips print each other's answers in both forms, and part 2's blanks are harder in B than in A.
All three problems are right and fair, but three problems on two mostly empty pages is too thin to judge a three-week unit: add a second problem to parts 1 and 2 and fit the check on one page.

The money gap is fixed (two money parts), but five of seven parts still need changes: part 6 does not check coin knowledge, part 4 B is easier and repeats A's story, part 2 B repeats A, part 5 A uses a Grade 1 time. Re-read after the rebuild.
All three earlier findings are fixed and keys are right. Part 1 can be done by elimination and has no pentagon; part 2 asks only faces.
All earlier findings are fixed and keys are right. Part 5 is a single coin-flip item, part 6 steps by 7 in every strip, and part 4's third problems differ in difficulty.

Parts 2-4 are below Grade 3 or uneven (whole-hour elapsed time, whole-hour addition in A, a fully labelled thermometer), the thermometer is Celsius only for a US check, and part 1's foils make the earlier time always right. Rebuild and re-read.

instruction.K-627: Circle ten squares. Write how many squares are outside your circle. Then write how many squares there are in all.
instruction.K-448: Count the dots in the two ten-frames. Write the number. Then finish the number sentence.
instruction.G1-275: Only 0, 10, and 20 are printed. Count on to each arrow and write its number.
instruction.G1-229: Count the coins. Write how much money there is in all.
instruction.G2-291: Find each thing on the price tags. Add the prices. Write the total.
instruction.G3-327: The numbers go down by the same amount each time. Write the missing numbers.
instruction.G3-344: Compare the two clocks. Write how much time passed.
instruction.G3-356: Start at the time on the clock. Add or subtract the time shown. Write the new time.
instruction.G3-345: Read each thermometer. Write the temperature in degrees Fahrenheit.
instruction.G2-263: Read the scale on each measuring cup. Write how many milliliters (mL) are inside.

worksheet: G2-518 Length Story Problems, answer key (all levels): the key writes the answer number into the bar box that the direction tells the child to mark with '?' (length-stories.js: key shows num(p.answer) where v is '?'), while the easier page's worked example shows '?'. Key should show '?' in the bar and the number only in the answer box; accept 75 - 28 = ? / 47 and 28 + ? = 75.

G3-344 How Much Time Passed? (all levels): every card is whole hours and the answer is 'hours passed'; 3.MD.A.1 measures time intervals in minutes. Add a minutes face (e.g., 3:15 to 3:50) and keep the cross-12 cards.

G3-345 Hot or Cold? (en): thermometers are Celsius only, while the lesson note's example is '70 degrees' and the platform already has G3-476 Degrees Fahrenheit. For en use degrees F (or a dual F/C scale asking for F).
G2-252, G2-260, G2-263 (en): British wording on an American page: 'Measuring Jugs to 2000 ml', 'Read the scale on each jug'. US: 'measuring cup', 'mL', '2,000'.

G1-229 Counting Money: All the Coins (en): direction says 'in each purse' with no purse drawn, and every coin carries its value as a numeral, so the page never asks which coin is worth what (the lesson note admits it).
G2-291 Shopping Math (en): 'Every card asks for a total.' is not classroom English; and the animals face prices live animals in cents.
G3-327 Going Down! (en): 'Write the missing ones.' reads as 'ones digits' to a Grade 3 child; say 'Write the missing numbers.'
K-627 Ten and Some More (en): 'Circle 10.' is heard as 'circle the printed 10'; say 'Circle ten squares.'
notes: Earlier review f1116, g2-measurement-time-money: (1) no money part: FIXED (parts 6 and 7). (2) right circle always the bottom one in part 2: FIXED (A bottom/top, B top/bottom), but B card 1 now copies A card 2. (3) part 4 key wrote the number where the child writes '?': FIXED in the check; still in the worksheet's own key (question 6). (4) form B repeats A's tape story with other numbers: NOT FIXED (same ribbon story, and now easier). (5) part 5 clocks: CHANGED, not fixed: the repeated :05 is gone, but A now has 12:30 and both card 1s are 9:05/9:10.

Earlier review f1116, g2-shapes-solids-symmetry: (1) no sorting-by-sides part: FIXED (part 1), with a new elimination tell. (2) symmetry direction: FIXED (part 3). (3) tangram direction: FIXED (part 5).

Earlier review f1116, g3-rounding-adding-subtracting: (1) chips in the same places in both forms: FIXED (write-in boxes). (2) part 1 two-digit Grade 2 line: FIXED (three-digit numbers). (3) part 3 repeats (totals 80/60, 43, fives in B): FIXED except both card 2s still total 60. (4) 190 - 158 with two boxes and the direction: FIXED. (5) within-20 balance part: RESOLVED by dropping 'Make it balance' (listed as not in the check). (6) ringed square for 'fill in the circle' and sums past 1,000: FIXED.
Every key answer in all seven checks was checked (arithmetic, clock-hand angles, ruler and unit counts, symmetry grids cell by cell, scale readings) and is correct.
The K check is 8 parts and 12 cards read aloud, three pages: long for one Kindergarten sitting. Suggest two sittings (parts 1-4 teen numbers, parts 5-8 counting).

Several checks leave most of a page empty: g2-add-subtract-within-1000 page 2 holds one problem; g2-shapes page 3, g3-rounding page 3, g3-time page 3 and g2-measurement page 4 hold one part each. Pack them; a shorter stack is easier to hand out.
Money notation: the cards print '25 ¢' with a space; US classrooms write 25¢.
g2-measurement part 7 B uses a persimmon, which most US second graders will call a tomato or an orange; harmless here (the child matches pictures) but a familiar fruit is better.
g3-rounding part 3 keeps two-digit addends; in a unit 'Within 1,000' three-digit addends rounded to tens (e.g., 238 + 452) would fit Grade 3 better.

questions.1: Not fair. 3.MD.A.1 is time intervals in minutes; 8:00 to 10:00 (and B's 4:00 to 7:00) is counting whole hours on the clock, Grade 2 work, and does not even cross 12, the lesson note's own watch point. Fix: draw from the level that crosses 12 (e.g., 11:00 to 2:00) and add one minutes card per form (A 3:15 to 3:50 = 35 minutes; B 9:40 to 10:20 = 40 minutes), direction 'Write how much time passed.' with the unit after the box. The worksheet G3-344 needs that minutes face too.
questions.2: Celsius only is wrong for a US Grade 3 check. US children meet temperature in degrees Fahrenheit (weather, classroom thermometers, NGSS weather data as US schools record it), and the lesson note's own example, '70 degrees', is a Fahrenheit reading. Use degrees F for en (G3-476 already draws it), or a dual F/C thermometer that asks for F. Also put the reading between labels (marks by 2, labelled every 10): today every mark is labelled. And 'ml' must be 'mL' everywhere (US and SI convention; the worksheet title already writes mL).
questions.3: Fair for this unit, with limits. K.CC.A.1 and A.2 are oral counting standards and K.CC.A.3 asks for writing numerals only to 20, so writing 42-80 goes past the K writing standard. But the unit's own lessons 5-8 teach exactly this, and each blank can be found by copying its neighbors' tens digit, so keep it, provided: every blank has a printed neighbor on each side (no three blanks in a row, as in part 7 card 2 of both forms); the teacher may accept a spoken answer or a reversed digit as counting-correct; and the answers are not printed elsewhere on the page (part 7 today). Let one part reach 100.
questions.4: No. With the value printed inside each plain circle, the part checks adding 25, 10, 5 and 1, not knowing the coins; the coins are also pre-sorted largest first, so 'start with the coins worth the most' is never shown, and 'purse' names nothing drawn. 2.MD.C.8 word problems are covered by part 7; this part should check coin values. Fix: coin faces (heads, grayscale, to scale) without numerals, in mixed order; if no coin art exists, write each coin's name (penny, nickel, dime, quarter) instead of its value. Direction: 'Count the coins. Write how much money there is in all.'
questions.5: Not acceptable as it stands. Same ribbon, same picture, same take-away frame, and B (72 - 20) needs no regrouping while A (75 - 28) does, so B is easier and a before/after gain is inflated. Keep the structure (whole known, piece cut off, result unknown) but change context, unit and numbers at the same difficulty: B 'A garden hose is 83 feet long. Dad cuts off 47 feet. How long is the hose now?' (83 - 47 = 36).
questions.6: Yes, a mistake a teacher would mind. The direction tells the child to write a question mark in the bar for the unknown length; the key fills that box with the number, and the easier page's worked example shows '?', so a child who did it right looks wrong against the key, and the key models the very confusion the lesson warns about. Fix the worksheet key as the check key now does: '?' in the unknown bar box, the number only in the answer box; for the equation accept 75 - 28 = ? (or = 47) and 28 + ? = 75.
